name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Saturday 19 November 1983

clue.text: They are in charge of studs

blocks.note: first meaning: people who run things, employers
second meaning: raised ornamental knobs on a surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'Studs' suggests a stud farm and its stallions, but here it means decorative knobs, which share a name with the people in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both employers or managers and the round raised knobs used as ornament on shields and ceilings.

clue.text: Similar offer partly rejected by word of mouth

indicators.note: partly means only a portion is used, a run of letters straddling the neighbouring words
something rejected is sent back, so the run of letters is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the letters straddle the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A matching bid was turned down in conversation rather than in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written, which is what passing something on by word of mouth means.

blocks.note: first meaning: astonished, taken aback
second meaning: arranged so as to start or occur at intervals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' allows that staggered times need not be strictly regular, only spread out.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggered is a past participle meaning both astounded and set out at intervals rather than all together.

blocks.note: surface reading: trills and other decorations added to a melody
setter's reading: gems used as jewellery

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: precious gems are ornaments, and the same word is short for a famous rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious gems set in jewellery are ornaments, and the band the Rolling Stones is commonly called by this short name.

clue.text: Pay others to relieve long standing strain

blocks.note: to foot a bill is to pay it
the rest are the others

explanation.surface: Someone hires help so they can stop shouldering a tiring burden themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's OCR reads 'relive'; the setter wrote 'relieve'. The definition is descriptive: a support you put your feet on after standing too long.
explanation.definitionFit: A footrest props up tired feet, easing the ache that comes from being on them for a long time.

blocks.note: Captain Cook called Tonga the Friendly Islands, so its people are cheekily described by that adjective
society is the fashionable upper class, as in high society

explanation.surface: A savings scheme set up for wealthy island residents.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the liberty of turning the people of the Friendly Islands (Tonga) into an adjective; the pieces come out in the reverse of their clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly society is a mutual association whose members pay in to insure themselves against sickness and old age.

clue.text: Above the head of ultimate superior

blocks.note: over means above
a lord is the head of a manor or household

explanation.surface: Someone placed over the boss is the final authority.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlord is a ruler holding supreme power over lesser lords, the one at the very top.

clue.text: Early article on an object of worship

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the object of worship comes first and the article goes under it

blocks.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
the definite article

explanation.surface: An ancient piece written about an idol.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the article below the god. Rathe is an old poetic word, as in Milton's 'rathe primrose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an archaic adjective for early or coming soon, used of flowers that bloom early in the year.

blocks.note: to state is to declare
mystery is an old word for a trade or craft, as in the medieval mystery guilds

explanation.surface: Someone announces the secret workings of politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is the art of governing a country, the skill of managing public affairs.

blocks.note: first meaning: an 18th-century dandy or fop
second meaning: a pasta dish on the menu

explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' is the old noun for a fashionable man, not the verb; the Macaroni Club dandies gave such fops this name, as in Yankee Doodle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the historical name for an overdressed fashionable young man and a familiar tube-shaped pasta served in eateries.

indicators.note: an unfortunate thing has gone wrong, so the word that follows is knocked out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A trap set to catch a hapless mother or father.
explanation.definitionFit: To snare and to entrap are both verbs for catching someone in a trap, literal or by trickery.

clue.text: New record covers for an old song

blocks.note: green means new or fresh
a vinyl record is kept in a cardboard sleeve

explanation.surface: A band brings out a new recording covering a traditional tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' tempts as the music-business sense, a new version of an old song; here it is literal packaging for records.
explanation.definitionFit: Greensleeves is a traditional English ballad from the sixteenth century, so it counts as a very old tune.

indicators.note: smitten means struck hard, so the two words before it are knocked into a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Oriel is head over heels for a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly smitten' reads as one phrase about love, but 'madly' is part of the letters and 'smitten' alone is the signal. Marie Lloyd was a famous English music-hall star.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Lloyd was a celebrated music-hall performer of the late Victorian era, known for comic songs.

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical marking for soft
a strain is a tune, as is an air

explanation.surface: A soft melody written for a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two matching things or people, a couple.

clue.text: They make bits of a footballer

blocks.note: first meaning: craftsmen who make bits, spurs and other metal fittings for horses
second meaning: more than one of footballer Peter Lorimer, the Leeds United and Scotland winger

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone hacking a player to pieces; 'bits' are the metal mouthpieces of a horse's bridle, and the second half wants the plural of a famous player's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorimer is an old trade name for a maker of horse bits and spurs, and Lorimer was a well-known footballer of the 1970s.

clue.text: Driver lacking experience but not colour

blocks.note: Stirling Moss, the British racing driver
green means new and inexperienced

explanation.surface: A novice motorist who is not yet up to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But not' reads oddly before the definition; it seems to tease that 'green' is used for inexperience, not as a colour, though the whole answer is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Moss green is a muted yellowish-green shade, named after the colour of moss.

clue.text: Feeling intense perhaps at the start

indicators.note: perhaps says the word before it is only one possible arrangement of its letters
the start of the following word is taken and added to the mix

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Emotion that runs strongest at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra letter is the start of 'the'; mixed with the seven letters before it, it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means able to feel or perceive, so as an adjective it matches feeling in the sense of sensitive.

blocks.note: first meaning: taking no notice, careless of
second meaning: senseless, done with no thought

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both paying no attention to something and acting with no intelligence or purpose behind it.

clue.text: There may be money in it that's for sure

definitions.text: There may be money in it

blocks.clueFragment: There may be money in it
blocks.note: first meaning: a strongbox for keeping valuables
second meaning: certain, as in a sure bet

explanation.walkthrough: 'There may be money in it' sounds like a business tip; it is the steel box itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe is a locked cabinet for cash, and safe also describes a sure, risk-free thing.

indicators.note: sounding means we judge the next word by how it is said, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: Finnish, from Finland, is one kind of foreign

explanation.surface: Wrapping things up with an exotic accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' is a broad hint: the specific nationality wanted is the one from Finland.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish is to end or complete something, and a finish is the end of a race.

clue.text: Hardly the person to wear indecent clothing

definitions.text: Hardly the person to wear indecent clothing

blocks.note: blue means risqué or smutty, as in blue jokes or a blue movie
a stocking is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A prim and modest person would never put on revealing outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer, and its last two words also build it: risqué plus a garment gives the name for a bookish woman, the last person to dress provocatively.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluestocking is a learned, studious woman, stereotyped as serious and unglamorous rather than flirtatious.

clue.text: Sacred writings are returned by the muse

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way they came, so both short pieces are read backwards

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament
taken as written

explanation.surface: Holy texts brought back by a source of inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Greek Muses, the one presiding over lyric and love poetry.

blocks.note: first meaning: a unit of land area
second meaning: the ancient harbour city in northern Israel

explanation.walkthrough: 'A measure of port' sounds like a glass of the fortified wine; port is a harbour town here.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, and Acre is a historic seaport on the coast of Israel.

blocks.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
an ace is the one in a deck of cards

explanation.surface: Sunshine is a source of cheer for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation, the comfort offered to someone in grief or distress.

blocks.note: first meaning: the title of a cardinal
second meaning: a rise or piece of high ground

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a person: a powerful cardinal is styled His Eminence, and the word can stand for the man himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence names both a high-ranking churchman and a raised area of land, an elevation.

indicators.note: laying a place waste wrecks it, so the city's name and the word before it are smashed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Greeks skilfully sacked the city of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid waste' reads as one phrase in the story of Troy, but 'laid' belongs to the letters and 'waste' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitly and dexterously are both adverbs for doing something with skill and nimbleness.

blocks.note: first meaning: a short sword that hung from the belt
second meaning: a wood on the side of a steep hill

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a wooden practice sword, but these are two separate meanings; in southern England a hanging wood on a slope is called a hanger.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger was a short sword worn hanging from a belt, and the same word is a dialect name for a hillside woodland.
